hit: The cell membrane is the cell wall and it controls what goes in and out.
the membrane is called the cell wall it lets things in and out

1.re: \bcontrol (?:center|centre)\b|\bbrain of the cell\b|\bcontrols? (?:all |everything |the whole )?(?:of )?(?:the )?cell'?s? (?:activities|actions|functions|jobs)\b|\bcontrols? everything (?:the cell does|in the cell)\b
1.say: Check that. The nucleus runs the cell. What does the membrane control at the border?
hit: The cell membrane is the control center of the cell.
the membrane controls all the cell's activities
it is the brain of the cell
miss: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
it decides what comes in and what goes out like a gatekeeper
the membrane regulates what gets into and out of the cell

3.say: Check that. The heads love water. Which part hides from the water?
hit: the heads hide from the water so they go in the middle
The heads avoid the water and the tails face out.
miss: There is water inside and outside the cell. The heads face the water and the tails hide in the middle away from the water.
water on both sides so the heads point to the water and the tails hide from the water
the tails avoid water so they stay in the middle and the heads touch the water

6.say: Check that. Does nothing get through, or only some things?
hit: Selectively permeable means nothing can get through, like a brick.
it means nothing goes in or out example a jar
miss: Selectively permeable means the membrane lets some things pass through but blocks others. Example: a colander lets water through but keeps the pasta in.
some things can get through but not others like a screen door
not everything gets through, like a strainer

7.say: Check that. What they need is a way through, not energy. What helps them cross?
hit: They need energy to get across because the tails are oily.
charged particles need ATP to cross the middle
miss: The middle of the bilayer is made of hydrophobic tails. It pushes charged and polar molecules away, so they need a transport protein to get across.
they need a protein channel to cross, not energy
they don't need energy to cross, just a carrier protein because the oily middle blocks them

7.say: Check that. The heads love water. Which part in the middle blocks charged particles?
hit: the heads block the charged particles so they need a protein
The phosphate heads push them away so they need help.
miss: The middle is the hydrophobic tails. It pushes charged and polar molecules away so they need a transport protein.
the heads are polar but the oily tails in the middle block them so they need a channel
the nonpolar tails repel them and a carrier protein helps them through

9.say: Check that. Oxygen gets in the same way you just defined. Which process is it?
hit: Diffusion is high to low concentration. Oxygen gets in by active transport.
particles move from high concentration to low concentration and oxygen gets into cells by osmosis
miss: Diffusion is when particles move from high concentration to low concentration. Concentration decides the direction. It needs no energy. Oxygen gets into cells by diffusion.
oxygen diffuses into the cell from high to low concentration
oxygen diffuses not osmosis, it goes high to low concentration

10.say: Check that. At equilibrium, is one side more crowded than the other?
hit: At equilibrium there are more molecules on one side but they keep moving back and forth.
one side has more concentration and the molecules keep moving
miss: At equilibrium the concentration is the same on both sides. The molecules do not stop. They keep moving back and forth across the membrane, the same number each way.
the concentration is equal so no side has more and they still move both ways
it is not more on one side, it is balanced and they keep moving back and forth

11.say: Check that. Pumps are active transport. What kind of proteins does facilitated diffusion use?
hit: Facilitated diffusion uses protein pumps to move glucose from high to low with no energy.
molecules go through a pump from high to low so it is passive
miss: Molecules that cannot get through on their own cross through channel or carrier proteins. It still goes high to low, so it uses no energy. It is passive.
it uses channel proteins and carrier proteins, not pumps, and it is passive
big molecules like glucose go through a carrier protein high to low with no ATP

12.re: \bfrom (?:the )?(?:side |area |place )?(?:with |that has |where there is )?(?:more|higher|high|most|lots of|a lot of) (?:solute|salt|sugar|stuff)\b
12.say: Check that. Water moves toward more solute. Which side does it leave?
hit: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a membrane. Water moves from high solute concentration to low.
water moves from the side with more salt to the other side through aquaporins
miss: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane. Water moves from where the water-to-solute ratio is high to where it is low, so it moves toward the side with more solute. Aquaporins are water channel proteins that let water in.
water diffuses across the membrane toward more solute through aquaporins
water goes from less solute to more solute through water channels

12.say: Check that. Aquaporins are channels. Does osmosis need a pump?
hit: Osmosis is water moving across the membrane toward more solute. Aquaporins are pumps that push water in.
water diffuses across the membrane and aquaporin pumps water into the cell
miss: Aquaporins are water channel proteins that let water in.
aquaporins are channels, not pumps, and water moves toward more solute
aquaporins are not pumps, they are tunnels for water

15.say: Check that. A pump costs energy. Is that active or passive?
hit: A protein pump is passive and moves molecules from low to high using ATP.
pumps are a type of diffusion that moves low to high with energy
miss: A protein pump moves molecules from low concentration to high concentration, against the flow. It needs energy (ATP) to do that.
a pump is active, it goes low to high and needs ATP
a pump is not passive because it moves against the gradient using energy
